steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir sausage in hot oil until crumbly and just slightly pink, about 5 minutes. Add potato and onion; cook, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and lightly browned, 10 to 15 minutes.
Stir in frozen vegetables and cook until heated through. Season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with Cheddar cheese to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Dinner Hash
raw_recipe.description: This easy hash recipe can be easily scaled to feed any number of people. I use it when it’s just my daughter and me home for dinner.
raw_recipe.name: Easy Dinner Hash

review.reviewBody: I enjoyed this dinner, but I was suprised by how dry it was. It needs a sauce similar to au gratin potatoes: I would like to see someone post a comment or new recipe that incorporates a sauce to bind these ingredients together. Since there is not much water, you have to be careful not to burn the sausage while you cook the potatoes. (I think it would be better to put the potatoes in a few minutes after the sausage has been cooking.) Also I used frozen hash brown potatoes to make it easier, but I should have put the onion in with the sausage, since it took longer to cook than the hash browns. To summarize: start the sausage and onion at the same time. Add the potatoes four minutes later with some kind of cheese sauce, then you would have a five star recipe.

I have found a solution to the dryness of this dish that others have encountered. While it does change it from a hash, it really does help hold it all together. I added one can of Campbell's healthy request broccoli cheddar soup and a 1/2 cup of milk after you brown everything. I stirred them both in, simmered until bubbly and then added frozen veggies and cooked until hot through. Very nice addition. You could also you cheddar cheese soup and adjust milk to your liking.

Cooked recipe tonight. Served with eggs. Husband loved it!. Cooked onions, sausage and chopped celery together. Added potatoes as recipe said. One thing I did was I cooked the mixed vegetables in microwave cook bag before I added them. Added them along with any water that cooked out of them. Turned burner down and covered and steamed a little. Added a little season salt and pepper. Before serving added cheese. Was moist and flavorful! Husband said he wanted to eat it again! Got a hug and he said that was good, which normally does not happen when I cook something!

I used hot Italian sausage. I also used yellow squash instead of the mixed vegetables and instead of dicing the potatoes and squash, I sliced them both thin and added a little minced garlic and J.O. spice. Nice easy meal.

Recipe is a great idea! I used ingredients on hand. Sauteed onions in bit of olive oil, added raw diced potatoe, sprinkled with pinch of sea salt and covered to cook until soft/crispy. Placed aside. In same skillet, browned Jimny Dean Reduced fat sausage. Added potatoes, mixed veggies from can & a bit of frozen chopped broccoli. Covered on low heat. Thx to other reviews, I topped hubby's serving with 2 fried eggs. Breakfast bliss for dinner. Thanks!

I added some oregano, garlic, and Worcestershire sauce with the recipe to give it a bit more flavor. Also used ingredients I had on hand already so I use Kolby Jack cheese from the block that I shred it along with the baby honey potatoes that I cut.
Pretty good, I added some more seasoning, and before I added the cheese I put 4 tablespoons of sour cream mixed it in really well. It was creamy and delicious.

This was a simple and hearty meal. Not to mention quick and yummy. I used ground beef instead of sausage and added red bell peppers to the mix. I also added garlic and other spices that I knew my family would enjoy. Needless to say, it was hit. Thanks for posting. As far as the recipe being a little dry, I guess you could use a little stock (of choice) or maybe a little tomato sauce to bind all the ingredients together. I did not need or use it, but I could see where some people may think that. Overall a good choice for dinner.

I used ground beef to make this recipe. I cooked the potatoes first- but not long enough (I'm impatient). Next time I'll probably boil them first then add them to the skillet. I also added some garlic to the potato and onion as they cooked. Other reviewers said the recipe was dry, so towards the end of cooking I added some milk to make a cheesy-type sauce and it turned out really tasty. I doubled the recipe to make enough for my family of 4 and it made at least 8 servings! So, I'd say the recipe as written will give you 4 servings.

Fixed this tonight for my husband and I and it was a success. I used some left over peas and added some fresh sliced mushrooms and a few tablespoons of cooking wine. I seasoned with peper and garlic powder, we love cheese so I doubled it that and this turned out very tasty. Quick and easy.

Yummy! I made this using lil smokies. I found that putting a cover on after adding the vegetables helped. The vegetables didn't seem to be getting hot at all until I did, and it also helped to melt the cheese too! I was so hungry after smelling it that I forgot to take a picture!

I made this recipe for a large group of Shriners. I received rave reviews. It was served with shredded cheddar jack cheese if they wanted it and had a simple mushroom gravy also. Served with cole slaw. It went over very well. I used half spicy Italian sausage and half regular italian sausage. There was a mild heat, but it was so good.
This was a great recipe! And it was easy to make.
Substituted Polska kielbasa for Italian sausage and added Cajun seasoning.
Great easy crowd pleaser! So many ways to add to it and change it up. Whole family loves it!

Easy dinner for two! I added fresh garlic that I fried with the onion. Then I later added basil, paprika, cayenne pepper, garlic salt (not a lot because kielbasa can be salty by itself), and pepper. Yum!

We love it! It's my husband's favorite. He suggested adding some scrambled eggs to it and it worked! I've used regular bulk sausage, a mix of regular and hot Italian sausage, and a mix of regular and chorizo sausages. All work great!
I'm not a big meat-eater, so I didn't include the sausage but it was still delicious. It was super quick and good leftover.
This was really tasty. I used turkey sausage seasoned with rosemary and added a can of diced tomatoes (drained). I'll definitely be making this hearty meal again.

If your hash is dry then add a fried egg or two! That yolk will add a nice creaminess for sure.Delish, used bacon instead of sausage and fresh veggies for the frozen which was chopped asparagus and bell peppers. SO GOOD!
